authority: Deterministic temporary battlefield sustainment at the 100-person command echelon. It moves conserved formation-custody stock between the fighting line and field HQ/baggage reserve and never creates personnel, ammunition, equipment, or mounts.

rules.ammunition: At contact start, anonymous/cohort missile troops have at most one registered carried load on the fighting line. Additional formation-custody war arrows or bolts remain at field HQ/baggage. A competent 100-person commander may send a bounded temporary carrier detail forward when ammunition is the only need and the rear route is secure; otherwise the hundred rotates rearward. If neither carried ammunition nor HQ stock exists, ranged fire is unavailable.
rules.equipment: A rearward 100-person element may replace battle-broken shield or armor components only from complete spare role-outfitting sets already in formation custody. Using a complete set removes it from the complete-spare count; no replacement is free.
rules.remounts: Replacement horses must already exist as formation-custody remount_horses. Lost active horses do not reappear. A serviced 100-person mounted element may draw available remounts and return later in the same battle.
rules.fatigue: Rearward elements gain bounded recovery credit while absent from contact. The rest credit can reduce battle fatigue gain but cannot erase the minimum fatigue cost of fighting.
rules.command: Routine resupply, relief and return are delegated to the 100-person command echelon. Higher and unit command quality controls how many hundreds can leave the line at once; local breaches reduce that freedom. This creates no persistent subunits.
rules.return: Serviced elements rejoin when their commander judges the line needs them. Under pressure they return promptly after service; with a stable line and high fatigue a capable commander may hold them rearward longer for recovery.

forward_ammunition.rule: When ammunition is the only material need and the rear route is stable, each 100-person commander may temporarily detail a bounded handful of its own bodies to carry arrows or bolts forward. This is not a new unit and does not permit equipment repair, remounting, or meaningful rest without a full rearward rotation.
